newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania miners strike over pay, leader's release.
newsitem.headline: Romania miners strike over pay, leader's release.

text.p: Thousands of miners went on strike in Romania's western Jiu Valley coalfields on Friday to demand pay rises and the release of their leader, who is accused of underminging state authority.
State television said talks between government negotiators and the striking miners were deadlocked.

In addition to hight pay, the miners want the immediate release of their boss, Miron Cosma, who is facing trial over his role in leading 1991 riots in which three people were killed when miners attacked government offices in Bucharest.

"Talks have hit a deadlock over the miners' pay claims and their demand that Cosma be freed from custody, which breaches the constitution," Vlad Rosca, the government trouble-shooter for labour conflicts, told state television.
Reformist President Emil Constantinescu has vowed to bring to justice those responsible for miner-led violence in 1991, when the first post-communist government was forced to quit.
The centrist government, which ousted ex-communists in elections last November, is pushing ahead with tough reforms, including closures in loss-making communist-era industries such as mining.
Miners earn about $100 a month, more than the average monthly pay of some $80, and they enjoy privileges dating back to the communist era, including discounts for rent, electricity and transport.

Trade and Industry Minister Calin Tariceanu described the strike as illegal, saying Jiu Valley coal mining was loss-making. "The Jiu Valley crisis is due to lack of efficiency of mining in the area," he told public television.
